title: Schema migrations 1 to 5 run outside a transaction and user_version is written only after all of them, so a crash during the first migration of a new or old database leaves a half-migrated file whose re-run fails (duplicate column, existing trades_new) and the bot cannot boot

evidence.note: v2: two ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with no existence guard and no transaction
v3: CREATE trades_new, INSERT, DROP trades, RENAME in one db.exec without a transaction
v6 and v7 (:221-228) are wrapped in db.transaction(); 1-5 are not
user_version is set once at the end, so any crash before it re-runs every step on the next import

sibling_sites_checked: Every migration block in db.ts:29-233. v4 (:113-118), v6 and v7 guard their ALTERs with PRAGMA table_info; v1 and v5 use CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS. The live database is at version 7 (AUD-FORENSIC-001), so only a database created or upgraded from now on is exposed; 22-09 moves migrateSchema verbatim into dbSchema.ts for npm run db:init (D-24), which keeps this behaviour. Multi-statement state changes outside a transaction in bot.ts (buy row, exit_state, lp_baseline) are SC-06 (BUY slice).
severity_rationale: S3: a boot-time crash-consistency defect with no capital effect at the base SHA (the bot refuses to boot rather than run on a bad schema); the v3 table rebuild without a transaction could lose the trades table only on a crash in the middle of that one historical step.
recommendation: Run each version step and its user_version bump in one transaction (and make v2 idempotent like v4/v6/v7); a pure robustness change with no behaviour change on a successful migration. Phase 29 (or with the 22-09 dbSchema move, which must stay verbatim per D-24).
